prompt.context: Your client, Congo.com (named after one of Earth's rainforests), is one of the largest e-commerce retailers in the world. It specializes in a diverse logistics network, and its brand is built around consumer satisfaction. The company has grown dramatically over the last 5 years, but has started to notice recent profit margin dips. You have been hired to find the root causes that Congo must address to focus on profitability so they can continue to drive growth.
prompt.question: Find the root causes of Congo.com's profit margin dips and recommend how they can improve profitability. Any positive change in profitability is the goal — quantify the impact of changes recommended.

clarifying_info.q: What markets or geographies are we focused on?
clarifying_info.a: Congo is a worldwide company, but wants to focus on US profitability to drive expansion into other countries.

clarifying_info.q: How does Congo define profit margin?
clarifying_info.a: Profit margin = net income / total revenue.

clarifying_info.q: How many distribution facilities does Congo have in the US?
clarifying_info.a: There are eight main distribution facilities in the United States.
Congo gives its customers the best prices with the fastest delivery rates. Company growth has outpaced all competitors in the retail industry.

clarifying_info.q: What is the goal — a specific margin target?
clarifying_info.a: Any positive change in profitability is the goal. It is up to you to quantify the impact of changes recommended.

exhibits.title: Congo.com Income Statement (US Distribution Centers only)
exhibits.shows: Annual income statement for Congo.com US operations from 2013 to 2017, showing units shipped, average revenue per unit, total revenue, and line-item operating expenses (Maintenance, SG&A, Transportation, Permitting, Other), as well as NI Pre-Tax, Taxes, and Net Income. All figures are unaudited and in millions.

exhibits.title: Congo.com US Distribution Network — 2017
exhibits.shows: A bar chart comparing 7 US distribution facilities (ABE8, AVP1, CLT2, CVG3, FTW1, MDW2, ONT8) across three dimensions: units per day, operating costs ($/day), and transportation costs ($/day). Square footage of each facility is also labeled (five at 500k sq ft, two at 1M sq ft).

data.note: Units per day, operating costs ($/day), and transportation costs ($/day) are shown as bars; exact bar heights must be read from the chart image.

exhibits.title: Trailer Utilization for Facilities Older than 5 Years
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis chart showing daily trailers shipped (bar, left axis) and trailer utilization percentage (line, right axis) from 2013 to 2017, covering facilities older than 5 years. A project proposal is shown alongside: automation upgrades would improve trailer utilization to company standards, cut transportation costs by 25%, and cost $10M per facility. A table lists each facility's age in years.

project_proposal.benefit: Cut transportation costs by 25% at eligible facilities
project_proposal.eligibility: Automation upgrades apply to facilities not built within the last 5 years

framework: Profitability = Revenue - Costs; diagnose whether the margin dip is revenue-driven, cost-driven, or both
Revenue drivers: units shipped (volume), average price per unit (mix/pricing)
Cost drivers: Maintenance, SG&A, Transportation, Permitting, Other — examine each as % of revenue over time
Identify which cost line is growing fastest as a share of revenue
Drill into Transportation: decompose into lane costs, trailer utilization, and US DOT costs
Evaluate facility-level efficiency: units per sq ft, operating cost %, transportation cost %
Quantify impact of targeted operational improvements on Net Income

questions.prompt: Review Exhibit 1. What is driving the profit margin decline from 2016 to 2017?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates quickly see that revenue grew 19% YoY (2016->2017) while Net Income fell from $651M to $300M. Transportation costs jumped from 50% to 60% of total revenue — the single biggest change. All other cost lines as % of revenue are flat or improving (Maintenance dropped from 10% to 5%; SG&A flat at 10%). Revenue per unit fell from $4.50 to $4.00 but Congo has little control over competitive pricing. The root cause is Transportation cost inflation.

math.setup: Net income margin = Net Income / Total Revenue
steps: Transportation cost growth: ($8,322-$5,812)/$5,812 = ~43% YoY vs revenue growth of 19%
math.answer: Profit margin fell from 5.6% to ~2.2%; Transportation costs (now 60% of revenue) are the primary driver.

questions.prompt: Review Exhibit 2. Which facilities are the biggest transportation cost opportunities?
questions.guidance: FTW1 ships more units per day than any other facility despite having only 500k sq ft (highest productivity: ~4 units/sq ft). AVP1 also has elevated transportation costs. Five of seven facilities have identical cost percentages (30% operations, 60% transportation). FTW1 and AVP1 stand out with 80% transportation cost percentage. Strong candidates note both FTW1 and AVP1 as improvement targets; bonus for also citing AVP1 despite its lower volume.

steps: FTW1: 500k sq ft, highest units/day -> ~4 units/sq ft (most efficient)
AVP1: 500k sq ft, moderate units/day -> ~3 units/sq ft
MDW2 and ONT8: 1M sq ft -> ~1–1.5 units/sq ft (less efficient)
Transportation cost %: FTW1=80%, AVP1=80%; all others=60%
math.answer: FTW1 and AVP1 have the highest transportation cost percentages (80%) and are the primary opportunities; FTW1 also has the highest productivity in the network.

questions.prompt: Given that transportation costs break down into lane costs, trailer utilization, and US DOT costs, and that Congo has been expanding shipping destinations, which sub-driver should be investigated?
questions.guidance: Lane costs and DOT costs should rise proportionally with destination expansion — they are expected. The anomaly is Trailer Utilization: if trailers are being sent partially filled, cost per unit rises disproportionately. Candidates should hypothesize that utilization is the controllable lever and ask to investigate it.

questions.prompt: Review Exhibit 3. What does trailer utilization tell us, and what is the financial impact of the automation upgrade proposal?
questions.guidance: Trailer utilization has remained around 40% in 2017 even as daily trailers shipped grew from 447 to 1407 (2013-2017). Only facilities older than 5 years (AVP1: 7 years old; FTW1: 8 years old) are eligible for the $10M automation upgrade. The upgrade cuts transportation costs by 25% at those facilities. Candidates should read daily transportation costs from Exhibit 2 for FTW1 ($1.6M/day) and AVP1 ($1.2M/day), apply 25% savings, and multiply by 350 operating days. Strong candidates identify both facilities.

math.setup: Annual transportation savings = Daily transport cost x 25% savings x 350 operating days
math.answer: Upgrading both AVP1 and FTW1 saves $245M/year in transportation costs and increases Net Income by ~60%, at a one-time investment of $20M.

questions.prompt: (Bonus/stretch) If automation improves trailer utilization from 40% to 60% in 2017, how many trailers would be needed per day?
questions.guidance: Use the concept that trailers carry a fixed volume of SKUs. At 40% utilization, 1407 trailers ship x units. Solve for volume constant, then recalculate trailers needed at 60% utilization.

math.setup: Volume constant = trailers * utilization; solve for new trailer count at higher utilization
math.answer: 1225 trailers per day (down from 1407), a reduction of ~182 trailers/day.

recommendation: Congo should invest $20M in automation upgrades at AVP1 and FTW1 (the two facilities older than 5 years)
This will reduce transportation costs by $245M/year, increasing Net Income by approximately 60% (from $429M to ~$674M pre-tax)
Congo should also study best practices from high-efficiency facilities (FTW1's 4 units/sq ft productivity) and apply them across the network to improve overall output
risks: Implementation costs ($10M per facility) and potential disruption to current operations during upgrade
Dependency on US Department of Transportation regulations and costs, which are outside Congo's control
Higher automation may increase maintenance costs over time
Partial trailer utilization problem may persist at other facilities even after upgrade
next_steps: Engage consulting firm to help renegotiate trailer contracts for better rates
Prepare distribution network infrastructure for higher utilization capacity and increased throughput
Evaluate remaining 5 facilities for future automation investment as they age past 5 years
Explore whether automation improvements can also reduce SG&A costs (headcount in facilities)
